note: bench:chat's questions on the repo's own fixtures (spec 8.13): the Abyss 13 to 11, built offline as test:valorantreview builds it and filled from its own Riot record, and the Split 13 to 7, asked of the player's upgraded review where their library has it (found by its map, score and mode, filled as 8.10 fills it) and otherwise built offline as test:riotreview upgrades the repo's 8.0.1 review, filled from Riot's record; and the lists every sheet's keys may name. The player's other matches have their own sheet in userData/bench/chat/questions.json, in the same shape. A key is written by hand from Riot's record of the round, beside its question, and checks the answer independently of the gates: `must` is what a right answer states, `mustNot` a claim it must not make (each one a wrong fact). A check is `any` (phrases, whole words, any case), `list` (a list below by name) or `re` (a regular expression with the samples it must and must not match, `pos` and `neg`, asserted before anything is sent). `atLeast` asks for that many of the phrases. `tag` puts a wrong fact under its bar: relabel, economy, meta, kit, map. `about: "round"`, on a check or on its list, reads only what is said of the round asked, never a clause quoting the match's counts, a hypothetical or advice (bench-chat.js roundText). `otherMatch: true` marks a check as markers of another match, and a phrase naming an agent the question's own match has is no marker of it (--dry names such a phrase). `open` is how the page is on the match: picked on the chip, newest (opened from the sidebar) or none (a general question). `expect` is the match the question must be answered on, and whether it moved the chip.
